clue.text: But does it make the government sweet?

definitions.text: But does it make the government sweet?

parts.words: But does it make the government sweet?
parts.note: the government's inner circle is its cabinet, and a sweet is a dessert course, so the clue asks for a pudding named after that body of ministers

explanation.definitionFit: This is a steamed dessert of bread or sponge with dried fruit, which shares its first word with a body of senior ministers.

clue.text: Gossip of Carrel's first party-member

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of the word Carrel's is used

parts.note: the Mad Hatter is a guest at the tea party in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A rumour about someone called Carrel's first political party member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party-member' suggests politics; it is the Hatter of the Mad Hatter's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk and tittle-tattle are synonyms for rumour-mongering chit-chat.

clue.text: Statistics of strikers?

parts.note: strikers suggests workers on strike, but here they are cricketers striking the ball, whose runs per innings are recorded

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, these figures give the mean runs a batsman scores per completed innings.

clue.text: Architect using northern wood

parts.note: ash is a timber tree and its wood

explanation.surface: A designer who builds with timber from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was the Regency designer of Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion.

clue.text: Sets out, most often, in summer

definitions.text: Sets out, most often, in summer

parts.words: Sets out, most often, in summer
parts.note: sets look like a verb meaning departs, but here they are the scoring units of a racket game mostly played outdoors in the warmer months

explanation.definitionFit: Matches in this racket sport are divided into sets and are mostly played on outdoor courts during the summer season.

clue.text: Such players are the first to court

definitions.text: Such players are the first to court

parts.words: Such players are the first to court
parts.note: court suggests wooing, but it is the playing court, where lower-ranked entrants play the early rounds of a tournament first

explanation.definitionFit: Players without a ranking placing in a tournament draw are thrown into the early rounds before the top names appear.

clue.text: Girl's hot-headed and liable to change into something more comfortable?

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, and with the possessive it gives DIS

indicators.note: headed means only the head, the first letter, of hot is kept
to change tells us the letters of liable are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman gets flustered and is inclined to slip into loose clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges LIABLE into ABILLE; the surface plays on the idiom 'change into something more comfortable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a state of being casually or partly dressed, as when relaxing at home in loose clothes.

clue.text: This danger's seen all over the place-but not by sufferers from this!

definitions.text: This danger's seen all over the place-but not by sufferers from this!

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: here the 's is a contraction of is, so its S counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A hazard visible everywhere except to people with a particular eye problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: those with this condition cannot see distant things, so they miss what is all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the condition of seeing near objects clearly while distant ones blur.

clue.text: Inspired roughly, being well-off?

definitions.meaning: inspired in its literal sense of breathed in, done noisily and harshly in sleep
well off read as well and truly off to sleep, deeply asleep, rather than wealthy

explanation.surface: Someone motivated in a rough way because they are rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing in with a loud rasp is what a deep sleeper does, and a sound sleeper is well and truly away.

clue.text: Skilled technician from Hobart is a newcomer

indicators.note: from signals the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the following words

explanation.surface: A trained tradesman who has recently arrived from Hobart in Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman or skilled manual worker is a synonym.

clue.text: Bear from America in disgrace

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a stain is a mark of disgrace on one's character

explanation.surface: A bear that has come from the United States in shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb, to endure or hold up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight or hardship is to uphold or endure it.

clue.text: Willowy spruce

definitions.meaning: willowy means slim and lithe, like the tree
spruce as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance

explanation.definitionFit: Slender and neat in appearance are both senses of this short adjective.

clue.text: One can not be trusted with matches, using air-ferries

definitions.text: One can not be trusted with matches

indicators.note: using signals the letters of the following phrase are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone untrustworthy around a box of matches travels by air ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately starts fires, so is the last person to give matches to.

clue.text: Seeking to improve ethical standards, trim social reform needed

indicators.note: reform needed tells us the letters of trim social must be reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A campaigner for higher morals calls for a tidy overhaul of society.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes a preachy concern with right conduct and virtue.

clue.text: For example: — Highland range?

parts.note: Highland is one of the Scottish local-government areas, and range is used in the sense of an extent of territory

explanation.definitionFit: Highland was one of Scotland's large administrative areas, and an area or zone is a synonym.

clue.text: Hemmed in, geese bid to break free

indicators.note: to break free suggests the letters of geese bid are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Trapped birds make an attempt to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounded by an enemy force, as a city under siege is, means hemmed in.

clue.text: One is seldom out of bounds in Victoria, for example

definitions.text: One is seldom out of bounds in Victoria, for example

parts.words: One is seldom out of bounds in Victoria, for example
parts.note: out of bounds suggests a forbidden area, but bounds are leaps, and Victoria is the Australian state, not the queen or the London station

explanation.definitionFit: This marsupial moves by hopping and is common across the Australian state of Victoria.

clue.text: To donate gratuitously, we hear, is a revelation

definitions.meaning: to hand over for nothing, said as the two-word phrase meaning to donate free
a revelation here is an unintended disclosure of a secret

explanation.surface: Hearing about a free gift turns out to be something revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken as two words it means to donate free; as a noun it is a telltale sign that betrays a secret.

clue.text: Baby-walker needs energy to pull

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in full of go
to cart something is to haul or pull it along

explanation.surface: A child's walking frame requires power to drag it along.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, a wheeled frame that supported a toddler learning to walk was so called.

clue.text: Number of eggs in a grip?

definitions.meaning: a set of eggs laid at one time by a bird

explanation.surface: Holding a set of eggs in one's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood of eggs laid together and a firm grasp share this word.

clue.text: Tackle degree of difficulty, taking day off

indicators.note: off, with taking, tells us the letter for day is removed

parts.note: hardness is the degree of how difficult something is

explanation.surface: Taking on a tough task by skipping a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb, to take on; it is the noun, equipment for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear, and the straps and fittings by which a horse pulls a cart are its gear.

clue.text: Trollope's caretaker?

parts.note: Anthony Trollope wrote a novel whose title character is a keeper of an almshouse, and caretaker suggests a custodian

explanation.definitionFit: This is a guardian or custodian, and the title of Trollope's first Barchester novel.

clue.text: Hospital record printed on ticker-tape?

parts.note: ticker suggests a stock telegraph, but it is slang for the heart, whose beat is traced on a paper strip

explanation.definitionFit: A tracing of the heart's electrical activity recorded on paper is this kind of chart.

clue.text: Czech river-or German

definitions.meaning: a river rising in the Czech Republic and forming part of the Germany-Poland border

explanation.surface: Asking whether a waterway is Czech or German.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flows from Czech hills to the Baltic, and the same word is German for the conjunction or.

clue.text: Excessively long mechanical device

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: A machine that is much too lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement or instrument is a synonym.

clue.text: Straight ruler-one who makes amends

parts.note: right can mean straight or direct, as in a right line
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, a ruler

explanation.surface: A straight ruler belongs to someone who puts things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick beside 'straight'; it is the monarch, ER = Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rights wrongs is one who corrects or redresses them.

clue.text: See where the bishop moves!

parts.note: see suggests looking, but a see is a bishop's area of authority, and the bishop moves about in it, not just on a chessboard

explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district under a bishop's jurisdiction.

clue.text: NHS policy, say, as ordered for treatment of repressions

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged afresh, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A health service rule decrees a course of therapy for buried feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Freudian therapy seeks to bring repressed thoughts from the unconscious into awareness.
